intro: わ and さ add no information; they colour a casual statement with the speaker's attitude. わ turns the sentence inward: it voices your own feeling, realisation or decision, almost as if talking to yourself out loud. さ shrugs it outward: it tosses a statement to the listener as something obvious or no big deal. Both belong to plain, casual speech, and neither ever asks a question.

skills.rule: End a plain-form sentence with a falling わ to voice your own feeling, realisation or decision: "I'm off, then", "wow, I'm tired".
skills.explain:
Modern spoken わ, said with a falling tone, is used by men and women alike: もう帰るわ (I'm heading home now), 疲れたわ (man, I'm tired), これは無理だわ (this is hopeless). It announces a decision you have just made or a feeling or discovery that has just hit you. It is very frequent in western Japan and common in Tokyo among friends.

A rising, sing-song わ (行くわ↗, 素敵だわ↗), often combined as わよ and わね, is the traditional feminine style. Today it sounds old-fashioned or theatrical and is mostly heard in fiction; you need to recognise it, not use it.

わ follows plain forms: verbs and い-adjectives directly (行くわ, 寒いわ), nouns and な-adjectives with だ (雨だわ, 大変だわ). It cannot follow a bare noun or な-adjective, and it never makes a question; for that you need か or の. Keep it out of polite or formal speech.

examples.jp: じゃ、先[さき]に行[い]く{わ}。
それはちょっと高[たか]い{わ}。
あ、雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ってきた{わ}。
今日[きょう]はやめておく{わ}。
examples.en: I think I'll give it a miss today.

contrast.note: ぞ is a rough, forceful assertion that pushes at the listener or rallies yourself: 行くぞ (come on, let's go!). わ is soft and self-directed: 行くわ (I'm off, then).
か asks: 帰るか? (shall we go home?). わ only states: 帰るわ (I'm going home). A question never ends in わ.
な also talks to yourself, but it muses or wishes: いいな (I wish I had that), 行きたいな. わ reports a realisation or decision: おいしいわ, これ (oh, this is good).

mistakes.bad: この花[はな]、本当[ほんとう]にきれい{わ}。
mistakes.good: この花[はな]、本当[ほんとう]にきれいだ{わ}。
mistakes.note: きれい is a な-adjective, so it needs だ before わ.

mistakes.bad: 明日[あした]、何時[なんじ]に来[く]る{わ}?
mistakes.good: 明日[あした]、何時[なんじ]に来[く]る{の}?
mistakes.note: わ never asks. A casual question ends in の or just a rising tone.

skills.tip: Could you say it to yourself under your breath? "I'm off, then", "wow, that's hard": わ.

skills.rule: End a casual statement with さ to toss it off as obvious or no big deal: "it's fine, you know", "that's just how it is".
skills.explain:
さ makes a plain statement sound offhand and self-assured: なんとかなるさ (it'll work out), 大丈夫さ (it's fine), 当たり前さ (that's only natural). It shrugs; the speaker treats the point as settled. It is casual and slightly masculine or cool in tone, but used by many speakers in Tokyo-area speech.

The key point of form: さ attaches directly to a noun or な-adjective with no だ. 学生さ, 大丈夫さ; never 学生ださ. Verbs and い-adjectives take it directly in plain form: 行くさ, 安いさ. It does not go after です or ます.

さ is also used in the middle of a sentence as a filler that holds the listener's attention, like "so, like": 昨日さ、駅でさ…. And it appears in retorts after question words: 何さ (so what?), それがどうしたのさ (what of it?). It never asks a neutral question on its own; that is か or の.

examples.jp: 大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]{さ}。
そんなの、当[あ]たり前[まえ]{さ}。
誰[だれ]だって失敗[しっぱい]はする{さ}。
気[き]にするなよ。また明日[あした]がある{さ}。
examples.en: Don't worry about it. There's always tomorrow.

examples.jp: 心配[しんぱい]ないよ。すぐ慣[な]れる{さ}。
examples.en: Don't worry. You'll soon get used to it.

contrast.note: わ is self-directed and needs だ after a noun: 大丈夫だわ. さ is aimed at the listener and drops だ: 大丈夫さ.
か asks: 大丈夫か? (are you OK?). さ answers with a shrug: 大丈夫さ (I'm fine).
かな wonders and doubts: なんとかなるかな (I wonder if it'll work out). さ is confident: なんとかなるさ (it'll work out).

mistakes.bad: 心配[しんぱい]ないよ。大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]だ{さ}。
mistakes.good: 心配[しんぱい]ないよ。大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]{さ}。
mistakes.note: さ replaces だ; it never follows it.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]、それは簡単[かんたん]です{さ}。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]、それは簡単[かんたん]です{よ}。
mistakes.note: さ is plain-speech only and cannot follow です. In polite speech use よ or no particle.

skills.tip: Can you shrug while you say it? Then さ, and drop the だ.
